findings.title: Case 25 demands unauthorized in-call owner re-activation and retry that contradicts the accepted design and has no production path
findings.evidence: tests/phase-6b-d110c-0c1f5b-integration-red.test.ts:943-945 issues once and requires the call to RESOLVE for all four non-`recoveryFails` combinations (`await issue`), while :954 requires the ambiguity-time handle to be deactivated (`currentEphemeralAuthority()` undefined), :963 requires `observed.planes.get(writer.databaseName)` to be a DIFFERENT handle, :971/:975 require every later commit and publication to run under that fresh handle, :989 requires the fence/replacement to be durably present exactly once, and :1008 requires the replacement's application effect. `observed.planes` is only written by the mocked `activateCreatorSuccessorAdoption` / `reopenCreatorSuccessorAdoption` (test :132) and `activateV3LivePlane` (test :280), so the handle can only change if a full plane re-activation runs inside the single public `issue()` call. The product cannot do this: `packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:6543-6548` sets `registration.operationAdmissionHalted = true` on `ISSUANCE_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN`, `:6403-6404` then fails every subsequent local issue with `v3 operation admission is halted until recovery`, and the flag is only ever reset by constructing a NEW registration at `:8467` (`activateV3LivePlane`). `examples/v3-room/src/index.ts` has no retry/rebind/reactivate path (only `reopenCreatorSuccessorAdoption` at :2341 during session creation and `activateCreatorSuccessorAdoption` at :4227 during `adoptCreatorSuccessor`). The accepted design says the opposite: `.logs/d110c-0c1f5b0r-design-3a156aca/design.md:389` — "transaction outcome unknown mid-plan | admission halts; reopen enumerates durable truth; no half-link exists" — and design RED case 25 (:529-530) — "admission halts; reopen finds either the row with its link or neither." The only place the in-call rebind-and-retry is stated is the REJECTED-run evidence `.logs/d110c-0c1f5b-red-1dcff170/assessment.md:65-70`, which itself labels it "a design/code clarification for later review, not a new API or a passing result." Grep of docs/production-hardening/production-hardening-tdd-plan-v2.md finds no signed case-25 clarification (unlike the case-24 clarification at 62f71f4d, plan lines 100370-100404).
findings.impact: To reach GREEN the parent must invent new room/Node lifecycle orchestration that, mid-public-call, deactivates a halted plane, re-acquires the module-global topic ownership in `packages/node/src/creator-adoption-activate.ts` (`activeOwners`, :73/:361-364/:426), re-authenticates the room-head floor and successor material, and replays a signed issue — exactly the class of recovery-adjacent ownership change the plan declares high risk and requires a separate reviewed prerequisite for (compare D.110c-0c1d, plan :100612-100622). The design's own stop rule (`design.md:552-561`) says to stop and reslice rather than fold such behavior in. As written the continuation is unreachable after a narrow GREEN, so this blocks GREEN either as an unauthorized scope expansion or as a fixture that cannot pass.
findings.required_action: Choose one and record it before GREEN: (a) obtain a signed, reviewed case-25 clarification in the D.110c-0c1f5b plan record (in the style of the 62f71f4d case-24 clarification) that authorizes a bounded in-call authenticated owner re-activation plus at most one signed retry, and specifies its ownership, idempotence and failure semantics; or (b) correct `ambiguousPlanIssue` so that all four non-`recoveryFails` combinations behave as the accepted design states — the ambiguous owner halts, `issue()` rejects, and recovery is demonstrated through an explicit `fixture.reopen` that enumerates durable truth — while keeping the existing exact row-and-link-or-neither, single-retry, no-duplicate-disposition and exactly-once-effect oracles.

findings.title: 60,000 ms single-`it` deadline is unvalidated for a 27-case plus 64-writer composition
findings.evidence: tests/phase-6b-d110c-0c1f5b-integration-red.test.ts:1750 sets `60_000` for one `it` that runs the main partial-progress scenario (3 closes), `sixtyFourWriterGoldenPath()` (64 room sessions, 256 routed application issues, 6 displaced sources, 3 closes/adopts, 189 `reopen(..., transfer=true)` calls each copying two whole IndexedDB databases at :617-624, a creator cold restart and a final cold reopen), then `sameKeyReentry()` (4 closes), `manualReviewHold()`, `creatorFenceScan()` x2, `delayedPublication()` x3, `displacedControls()`, `staleLocalHead()`, `ambiguousPlanIssue()` x5 and `positiveAuthenticatedPruning()` (3 closes). The one executed calibration point is the v1 control: 1532.146791 ms for 2 rooms, 3 peers, 4 closes, 4 adopts and 3 reopens (.logs/d110c-0c1f5b-red-cecde972/result.json:35). `.logs/d110c-0c1f5b-red-cecde972/assessment.md:59` states plainly: "No source inspection can establish total GREEN wall-clock cost; RED is not a claim that the unexecuted continuation meets that deadline."
findings.impact: If the composition exceeds 60 s the GREEN run fails on a fixture deadline rather than product behavior, forcing yet another tests-only correction commit and re-run — the exact loop that already produced two rejected runs (`1dcff170`, `8fcbc039`).
findings.required_action: Owner: the tests-only correction that addresses the P1. Disposition: set the `it` deadline from the measured cost of the 64-writer path (or split the composition into a second `it`), and record the measurement in the GREEN evidence. Do not change any product parameter, `maxEpochVertices`/`maxEpochBytes`, the 5,000 ms routed-ack guard, or the store page ceilings to make it fit.

findings.title: Non-creator rollback-generation retention is a byte copy of the creator's AHE database, not independent per-peer evidence
findings.evidence: tests/phase-6b-d110c-0c1f5b-integration-red.test.ts:617-622 `reopen(..., transfer=true)` calls `transferDatabase(`${origin.databaseName}--ahe`, `${peer.databaseName}--ahe`)`, and `transferDatabase` (:366-375) does `owner.clear()` then re-puts every row of every object store — so the receiving peer's own AHE generation lineage and head are destroyed and replaced with the creator's. `positiveAuthenticatedPruning` (:1302) reopens `peers[1]` with `transfer=true` and then asserts `assertRetainedRollbackPair(peer)` for BOTH peers (:1343), and `sixtyFourWriterGoldenPath` reopens all 63 non-creators with `transfer=true` (:1241). `assertRetainedRollbackPair` (:843-859) reads exactly the copied rows.
findings.impact: `F5B_C13_C24C_EXACT_TWO_SUPERSEDED_ROLLBACK_GENERATIONS` and the two-level `baseExpectedHead` walk are tautological for non-creator peers: they re-read the creator's generation rows rather than proving that the peer's own successor staging/complete/swap produced and retained its own two `Superseded` rollback generations. The per-peer issuance/plan/prune oracles remain genuine (issuance and journal are not copied), so the loss is confined to case 13/24c's rollback-retention half.
findings.required_action: Owner: parent f5b GREEN evidence. Disposition: either assert `assertRetainedRollbackPair` only for the creator (whose AHE is never overwritten) and state explicitly that non-creator rollback retention is inherited transport state, or capture one non-creator peer that reopens WITHOUT `transfer=true` after it has independently adopted, and assert its own lineage there. Do not weaken the existing creator-side assertions.

causal_red_assessment:
The accepted RED is genuinely causal. `.logs/d110c-0c1f5b-red-cecde972/result.json` records one execution, runner status 1, two selected tests in one file, 1 failed / 1 passed, zero skipped/todo, zero top-level errors, no additional soft failures. The sole failure is `F5B_SETTLEMENT_PROFILE_SUCCESSOR_CODEC_REQUIRED: genuine settlement successor fails CERTIFIED_VALUE_MISMATCH before checkpoint production`, thrown at test :684 from the `close()` helper at :1672 after 417.58 ms.

The chain is real product, not a missing import/export or setup error. `openRoom(2)` builds a genuine genesis invite with `profileId: "creator-trusted-settlement-v1"` and a version-3 latched ACL (accepted today: packages/protocol-v3/src/latched-acl.ts:145 allows 256 members at version 3, :254 gates version 3 on `settlementProfileFor(...) === "v1"`). The test performs real issue, real publication through the transport, real creator ingress with awaited admission acks, and a genuine published displaced two-intent batch (`F5B_REAL_BATCH_SOURCE`, :1666) before calling `sealEpoch()`. The failure originates in production: packages/protocol-v3/src/creator-close.ts:276 (`prepareCreatorAnchorSigningRequest`) requires the literal `creator-trusted-v1`, which the seal actor maps to `CERTIFIED_VALUE_MISMATCH`, and packages/node/src/creator-close.ts:1031 throws `creator close actor failed: CERTIFIED_VALUE_MISMATCH`. The helper catches only that exact string and rethrows the labelled token; it substitutes no profile, checkpoint, signature, actor result or authority.

The five hard-coded profile sites the test pins all exist as claimed and are genuine (not synthetic-success adapters): creator-close.ts:276 (`profile.profileId !== "creator-trusted-v1"`), :541 (`profileId: "creator-trusted-v1"` in `completeCreatorSuccessor`), :598 (`decodedRecord.profileId !== "creator-trusted-v1"` in `openCreatorSuccessorTrust`), creator-checkpoint.ts:144 (`decoded.profileId !== ...` in `trustRecord`) and :242 (reconstructed genesis record). All five source-attribution assertions ran to completion before the throw, per the reporter timing and both rejected-run assessments.

No forged record, substituted checkpoint or fixture-only trust exists. `checkpoint()` (:704-748) reads the real proposed closure captured from `inspectCreatorTransitionAdvance` and opens it with the production codec `openCreatorAuthorSettlement` under `advance.successorTrust` as `floorTrust`; the codec's `OPEN_KEYS` (packages/protocol-v3/src/creator-author-issuance-frontiers.ts:43-51) matches the seven keys the test passes exactly, and it independently re-verifies the ed25519 signature and every binding. `F5B_C26_FLOOR_ONLY_CHECKPOINT_OPEN` and `F5B_NO_LEGACY_CONTROLS` are real product oracles. The v1 control also observed a genuine production string, `v3 room successor reopen failed: D110C_FLOOR_MISMATCH: creator successor differs from the authenticated room-head floor`, which matches packages/node/src/creator-adoption-activate.ts:447/:502 wrapped by examples/v3-room/src/index.ts:2362.
coverage_assessment:
The continuation covers the parent-owned matrix substantially better than the superseded `3a9e9329` attempt, and the two prior Sol P1s (missing parent composition cases; inadequate 64-writer oracles) are materially closed.

Verified present and correctly constructed: case 1 (`F5B_C01_DELAYED_DEPENDENCY_NOT_ADMITTED`, :1674); 2/3/10 (fence-precedes-replacement at :1688, committed-prefix crash at :1683, unlinked-suffix-once at :1722); 4/15/16/19 in `delayedPublication` for all three modes, including `F5B_C16_NEXT_EPOCH_LARGER_FENCE` and `F5B_C15_DISPLACED_REPLACEMENT_BECOMES_SOURCE`; 5/11 manual-review hold with a durable unfenced plan and a proof that only the held author stalls (:1533-1538); 6-9 same-key reentry across three absent closes, new incarnation `[author, 4, null]`, never-reset device sequence, empty-plan-still-fences, fresh-device fence at slot 0, and a real stale-envelope ingress rejection; 12/23 adversarial creator fence scan; 13 negative (:1704-1709) and positive; 14 three transitions plus cold reopen; 20/21 displaced controls; 22 genesis incarnation; 24a/24c; 25; 26 in-test plus f5b0a.

The adversarial fence scan is genuinely sound: `makeFence(10_002, 10_003)` is rejected at ingress by production authentication (packages/protocol-v3/src/index.ts:3533-3539 refuses a fence whose `fenceSequence > authorSequence`), so the contiguous scan legitimately stops at 10_001 rather than crossing into slot 10_002 — the expectation matches design steps 2 and 4 exactly.

Non-duplicated cases are cited to closed owners and every citation checks out: cases 18/26/27 to tests/d110c-0c1f5b0a-settlement-codec-red.test.ts:540, :491 and :524, and interrupted pre-floor adoption to tests/phase-6b-d110c-0b0a-staged-handoff-red.test.ts:162 and :246 — all four titles exist verbatim.

Gaps: case 17's `creator-trusted-v1` half is ungated (P2), and case 5's absent-plan/already-fenced refusals are covered by closed f5b0s tests but not cited in the ownership map (P2). Checkpoint-derived reachability for `openProgressSources` is genuinely required by the fixture: `F5B_AUTHENTICATED_SOURCE_IS_TERMINAL` (:1694) places the source at or below `terminalThrough`, so the later `F5B_OPEN_PROGRESS_SOURCES_AUTHENTICATED_FRONTIER_REACHABILITY` (:1715) can only pass if `openProgressSources` (packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:8822-8827, consumed at :7054) is actually consulted — the frontier's stated obligation is met, not evaded.
realm_assessment:
The per-peer `creator-adoption-activate` query-isolated import is a faithful model of independent physical clients, and I found no bypass or false-positive route.

The guard being isolated is genuinely module-local: `activeOwners` is a module-scope `Map` at packages/node/src/creator-adoption-activate.ts:73, read at :361 and written at :403/:426, with the "creator successor already has a conflicting active owner" refusal at :364. In production, independent devices are independent processes with independent module state, so one realm per physical peer is the correct model — the rejected run `1dcff170` proved the un-isolated fixture collided precisely there, and `8fcbc039` proved the isolation resolves it (the v1 control then advanced past the first non-creator reopen).

Production source is preserved: the mock imports `../packages/node/src/creator-adoption-activate.ts` with a `?f5bClient=<peerId>` query — the same unedited source file, not a rewrite. Vite does not propagate arbitrary queries to a module's own imports, so the realm's `import "./creator-adoption.js"` and `./internal/creator-adoption-intent.js` resolve to the single shared instances; opaque intent custody, handle aliasing and recovery dependencies keep exact identity, as the mock's comment claims.

The export surface is fully covered with no leak: `creator-adoption-activate.ts` exports exactly `activateCreatorSuccessorAdoption` (:435) and `reopenCreatorSuccessorAdoption` (:457), and examples/v3-room/src/index.ts:8-11 imports exactly those two. Both are wrapped by `capture`, so there is no path where ownership is registered in realm X but released through the shared module. Release stays correct because the wrapped `deactivate` closure installed at :250-263 is captured inside the owning realm, so `room.close()` deletes from the right map.

Opaque capability identity is preserved — `capture` passes the caller's original input object through unchanged and returns the real result; no handle, capability, checkpoint, floor or activation result is substituted. Same-peer restart ownership is preserved because `realms` is keyed by `peerId` and never cleared or reset, so a peer keeps one realm across every close/reopen; the singleton guard therefore still operates within each client. The transport-identity assertion at :126-128 pins `peerId` to the exact `d110c-f5b-parent-<n>-peer-<n>(-fresh)?` shape, and the cross-realm identity check at :117-120 positively proves distinct function identities per peer.

Residual notes, not findings: the isolation necessarily removes any cross-client `navigator.locks` dimension (the rejected assessment states this honestly — "not a claim of separate OS processes, independent browser globals, or a cross-window Web Lock test"), and no assertion positively demonstrates that a same-peer double activation is still refused within one realm — the guard is preserved structurally but not exercised.
golden_path_assessment:
The 64-writer composition is a genuine one-room product golden path, not a membership count.

One real room: `openRoom(64)` builds a single objectId with one version-3 latched ACL carrying 64 ACL-authorized members (index 0 admin/finality/writer, the rest writer), and `F5B_64_EXACT_PRODUCT_ACL_AFTER_RECOVERY` (:1079) re-asserts the exact product ACL for every peer in every epoch. `F5B_64_AUTHENTICATED_ACL_MEMBER_VECTOR` (:1189) pins 64 checkpoint frontiers.

Every writer really issues, is admitted, applies and publishes in each of epochs 0-3: per-author exactly-one issued operation (:1092), issued in the current epoch (:1094), backend-confirmed publication via the real `compareAndMarkOutboxPublished` observer (:1097-1105), creator-authenticated admission ack via `onAcceptedVertex` (:1106), and the author's own product state containing its own operation (:1109). `F5B_64_PER_AUTHOR_FOUR_EPOCH_ACCOUNTING` (:1251-1254) requires `[0,1,2,3]` for all 64. Accounting is exact and self-consistent: 256 contributions (:1244), six displaced sources (:1245), 268 `wide-` application operations across all commits (:1273-1278 = 256 + 6 sources + 6 replacements), 262 unique final effects (:1279), per-author hole-free device lineage against real `readLineage` (:1257-1260) and per-author publication conservation (:1267-1270).

Rotating offline cohorts are correct and disjoint: `peers.slice(1 + epoch*8, 9 + epoch*8)` gives indices 1-8, 9-16, 17-24 — eight each, all having already contributed in that epoch before `fixture.stop`, remaining stopped across close, checkpoint and adopt plus the selected epoch-1 creator cold restart (:1229-1234, which re-asserts exact product state, identical authority and preserved active head), then rejoining before the next epoch's issue (`F5B_64_REJOIN_CONTRIBUTES_BEFORE_NEXT_CLOSE`, :1117). Selected displaced work is both pending and published (:1180 — one held/published, one publication-failed/pending), and each is recovered with a real `transform` disposition, fence-before-replacement order and exactly one replacement link (:1143-1151).

Links are all real: contiguous anchor lineage (:1199), adjacent checkpoint digest (:1202), monotone history size and advancing history root (:1205-1210), successor anchor/ACL bound to product authority (:1216-1217), `F5B_64_SETTLEMENT_AUTHORITY_NO_DOWNGRADE` (:1123), snapshot cut binding the exact sealed state digest (:1190), and a semantic digest under `ts-drp/state/v3` (:1160-1163), plus a final creator cold reopen re-deriving the exact state (:1280-1283). Three monotone transitions `[1,2,3]`, monotone floor epoch and monotone active-head revision satisfy 24c (:1218-1249).

Two limits are worth recording, neither a defect against this design: non-creator peers never receive each other's vertices (the transport routes only to peers[0]), so cross-peer convergence happens through snapshot recovery rather than gossip — consistent with the design deferring non-creator hot follow to D.110c-c; and the whole-`--ahe` transfer weakens per-peer rollback-retention evidence (reported P2). The fixture is correctly scoped as three wide transitions, explicitly not the later ≥100-transition campaign (:20-22).
scope_api_assessment:
The narrow GREEN is implementable with no new public API, wire, schema, cryptographic, dependency or threshold change — with the single exception of the P1 case-25 behavior, which is a lifecycle scope expansion rather than an API change.

Minimal allowed production seams, all confirmed against current source:
1. Five profile literal sites, replacing the hard-coded comparison with the existing exported `settlementProfileFor` predicate: packages/protocol-v3/src/creator-close.ts:276, :541, :598 and packages/protocol-v3/src/creator-checkpoint.ts:144, :242. No new export is required — `settlementProfileFor` already exists and is already consumed by latched-acl.ts:3/:254 and creator-transition-advance.ts:795/:888.
2. Settlement checkpoint composition in packages/node/src/creator-close.ts: emit one `drp-creator-author-settlement-state` candidate and no legacy retirement/aggregate, and replace the close-aborting `AUTHOR_REENTRY_PROOF_REQUIRED` path at :530-541 with the design's fence scan under the profile only. The codec (`openCreatorAuthorSettlement`, `frontierFor`, `frontierCount`) and the advance predicate's settlement branches (creator-transition-advance.ts:795-822, :888) already exist from the closed f5b0a slice; the close-side producer is what is missing.
3. Authenticated frontier threading: packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:8242 currently calls `readSettlementSources(registration)` with no second argument, so `settlementFrontier` is always `undefined` and the function short-circuits at :8808 — `openProgressSources` (:8822) is presently dead. GREEN must thread a checkpoint-derived `SettlementFrontierContext` (the type and its validator already exist at :4932) into that call and the classification paths at :4794/:7044.

Existing-input close rebind: examples/v3-room/src/index.ts:1531-1537 currently throws `v3 room successor authority composition is unsupported` for `successorSnapshotDeclaration` + `creatorFinalitySigner`. Relaxing this under the settlement profile and rebinding close authority after authenticated reopen uses only inputs already on the public `CreateV3RoomSessionInput` shape; it is an input-acceptance change, not a new carrier. It must not weaken the non-genesis floor check at :1630-1636.
5. Authenticated prune ownership: today `planClosedEpochCleanup` (packages/node/src/internal/closed-epoch-cleanup.ts:442) has no production caller, and the only production call to `maintenance.pruneAuthenticatedSettledPrefix` is the post-hoc REPLAY verification at v3-live.ts:3213, which explicitly fails if it deletes anything (:3222-3228). GREEN must add the first deleting invocation on every peer after verified adoption, rollback retention, availability and expected-head checks. This is the reachability the f5b0d reslice (`adab0f56`) moved to the parent, and it needs no new API — `durableIssuancePruningMaintenanceForStore` and the maintenance capability already exist.

The test's prune observation is correctly attached to the real owner and does not mint a capability: `browserIssuancePruningMaintenanceForStore`'s capability delegates by late property lookup (`(input) => implementation.pruneAuthenticatedSettledPrefix(input)`, browser-issuance-store.ts:1398), so `vi.spyOn(implementation, ...)` at test :254 intercepts the genuine production call chain while calling the real bound method; the WeakMap facade identity is preserved because the mock returns the same store object with `Reflect.set` patches. `F5B_C13_PARENT_IS_FIRST_DELETING_MUTATION_NOT_RECEIPT_REPLAY` (`deletedAuthorSequenceRange.from === 0`, :1313-1316) correctly distinguishes the first deleting mutation from the v3-live.ts:3213 replay, which by contract can only return a null deleted range.

Closed store/page contracts are respected without raising any ceiling: the corrected `durable()` helper (:768-792) pages with `limit: 128`, exactly `MAXIMUM_DURABLE_ISSUANCE_PAGE_LIMIT` (packages/issuance-store/src/types.ts:18), using the exclusive `[objectId, author, lastSequence]` cursor until exhaustion with strict-progress and exact-scope assertions; `aheFacts` uses `limit: 64` within the same maximum and follows `nextCursor`. `SETTLEMENT_REPLACEMENT_MAX_INTENTS = 16` and the `replacementProgress` chunk shape the test relies on already exist (types.ts:50-76, contract.ts:418-468).

Bounded, deterministic and reachable after GREEN: yes for every continuation except case 25 (P1) and subject to the deadline risk (P2). One structural expectation worth naming: `assertRetainedRollbackPair`'s exactly-two-`Superseded` invariant is self-consistent only if the cleanup plan's `deleteGenerationIds` prefix deletion runs synchronously inside the creator's `adoptCreatorSuccessor()` — genesis leaves exactly one `Superseded` (the anchor-trust generation from control-plane/src/anchor-trust.ts:639 superseded by the live-plane staging at v3-live.ts:2661), the first adoption makes two, and each later adoption makes three unless the floor prefix is deleted. `planClosedEpochCleanup` refuses with `D109A_ROLLBACK_INSUFFICIENT` below two ancestors (closed-epoch-cleanup.ts:279-295, :477), so the GREEN invocation point is constrained; it is achievable but should be stated explicitly in the GREEN plan.

Accepted run: `.logs/d110c-0c1f5b-red-cecde972/` classifies itself `ACCEPTED_CAUSAL_RED_PENDING_REVIEW` with executionCount 1, runnerStatus 1, 2 selected tests in 1 file, 1 failed / 1 passed, 0 skipped, 0 todo, empty `topLevelErrors`, empty `additionalSoftFailures`, one failure message total and empty metadata on both assertions. `commands.json` records a single `vitest run` invocation from the signed, pushed tests commit `cecde972` on base `aea679ba`, with `productionEdits: 0`, `planEdits: 0`, `longRuns: 0`, 27 stashes preserved, and it honestly flags two diagnostic `rg` command errors as command errors rather than test executions. The result carries an explicit warning that post-causal continuations did not execute and no GREEN or golden-path claim is made.

Rejected runs are correctly distinguished. `1dcff170` (`REJECTED_MATRIX`) is 2 failed / 0 passed: the intended settlement token plus a v1 control that failed on `authority-unavailable: creator successor already has a conflicting active owner` — its assessment names the exact realm collision at creator-adoption-activate.ts:73/:360-364 and records that `D110C_FLOOR_MISMATCH` was NOT runtime-observed. `8fcbc039` (`REJECTED_MATRIX_STOPPED_NO_RERUN`) is also 2 failed / 0 passed, with the v1 control failing on `DurableIssuanceTypeError: page limit is outside the closed range` at browser-issuance-store.ts:1210 because the helper requested 256 against the product maximum of 128; the assessment names the correct fix (page with 128 and the cursor) and explicitly refuses to raise the product ceiling. Both are labelled REJECTED, both record that the stop rule fired, and both preserve the prior review union (Sol FAIL with two P1s, Fable xhigh PASS with three P2s, Grok `NO_VERDICT_TIMEOUT` treated as neither finding nor approval). The earlier `0c59869a` rejection is likewise recorded inside `3a9e9329/assessment.md`.

Exact test counts and the raw reporter matrix check out against the file itself: `list.json` shows exactly two tests in one file, matching the single `describe` and two `it` blocks at :1653/:1654/:1752.

Static/type evidence: `typecheck.json` shows `targetDiagnostics: []` and three inherited `tests/fixtures/phase-4b-v3/live-snapshot.ts` diagnostics (2741, 7006, 2322), honestly labelled as not a full-repository typecheck pass. The 2322 diagnostic is a real fixture drift (the mock's `transactWriteSettlementPlan` returns `SettlementPlan | null` against the contract's `SettlementPlan`); it is pre-existing, type-only, and the file is imported here solely for `fakeNetwork`, so it does not affect this RED.

Manifests: `.logs/d110c-0c1f5b-red-cecde972/manifest.sha256` is self-excluding with 11 entries and structurally covers exactly the 11 non-manifest files present in the root; the accepted design root `.logs/d110c-0c1f5b0r-design-3a156aca/manifest.sha256` lists its three artifacts (design.md, pre-review.md, next-prompt.md) and the design cited is the f5b0r grammar, not the superseded f5b0/f5b0p/f5b0q families.

Limitation I must state plainly: this session has no shell, so I could not execute `sha256sum` to verify any manifest digest, nor `git verify-commit`/`git log --show-signature`/`git status` to independently confirm GPG signatures, pushed-ref identity or changed-path custody. Those three properties rest on the self-reported `commands.json` entries (signature `G`, `aea679ba..cecde972` push, `git commit --only <test path>`, `git diff --check` exit 0) and on the assessments' claims of a 14-insertion/1-deletion tests-only diff. Everything I could check by reading — file inventories against manifests, reporter counts against the test file, every cited product line, every cited retained-test title, and every error string — matched.
